primary_findings: The explicit registry-gap D-law fixed the Probe 014 failure: all four outputs kept canonical_semantic_pointer null.
Both bait variants rejected nearest-class repair to ui.menu and rejected promoting CREATE ui.toast@v3 into canonical_semantic_pointer.
All four outputs independently nulled canonical_object_class and object_version, which confirms that these fields are being read as canonical-admission fields rather than parsed raw candidate fields.
This suggests the next schema should split raw_object_class_candidate / raw_object_version_candidate from canonical_object_class / canonical_object_version.
evidence_boundary: Probe 015 proves explicit D-law is enough for sparse registry-gap remand in these four specimens.
Probe 015 does not prove natural semantic binding at scale.
Probe 015 shifts the recommended schema interpretation: registry_gap should null all canonical admission fields while preserving raw candidate fields separately.
recommended_next_iteration: Add raw_object_class_candidate and raw_object_version_candidate to the resident body shape.
Keep canonical_object_class and canonical_object_version null under registry_gap unless registry authority exists.
Run a follow-up with the split raw/canonical object fields before moving to hidden-route binding.
overall_assessment: Probe 015 converts the Probe 014 failure into a clear D-law pass. The stronger lesson is schema-level: raw semantic preservation needs separate raw candidate fields; canonical fields should remain null under registry gap.
